reasons: Only 7 of 12 sections were available, so the status cannot cover the whole file.
Pin failures are logged to the console only, with no message to the user.
The page relies on the backend returning the right type names for filtering.
No tests are visible in the reviewed parts.

terms.meaning: a list of health events in date order
a button that narrows the list to one kind of event
marking an event so it is kept at the top of the view
a fixed list that matches each event type to its icon, colour and label
narrowing the results on the backend before they reach the screen

used_by: Next.js route for the health timeline (apps/web/src/app/(dashboard)/timeline)

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the timeline page
sections.what: Brings in icons, layout pieces, the notification helper, the API helper and date formatting tools.

sections.name: TimelineEvent
sections.title: Shape of one timeline event
sections.what: Defines the fields an event carries: id, type, title, description, severity, when it happened, whether it is pinned, and an optional linked document.
sections.why: Gives one common shape so every event is shown the same way.
sections.watch_out: Severity has only four allowed values. A new value from the backend would not match the rules here.

sections.name: TimelineSummary (part 1)
sections.title: Summary shape and event type styles
sections.what: Defines the summary counts (total, recent, critical flags, last update, count per type). Also starts a lookup table that gives each event type its icon, colours and label, such as Document or Lab Report.
sections.why: The lookup table keeps the look of each event type in one place.
sections.watch_out: Any event type missing from the lookup table would have no icon or label, so keep the table in step with the backend.

sections.name: TimelineSummary (part 2)
sections.title: Rest of the event style lookup
sections.what: Finishes the lookup table with the styles for doctor notes, routine milestones and the other event types.
sections.why: Completes the mapping from event type to display style.
sections.watch_out: Some labels are reused across types, such as Lab Report and Routine both using teal, so users may find styles hard to tell apart.

sections.name: filterTabs
sections.title: Filter tab list
sections.what: Lists the filter tabs shown above the timeline: All, Documents, Vitals, Medications, Symptoms, Conditions and Doctor Notes.
sections.why: Gives the user quick ways to narrow the history by kind.
sections.watch_out: Filter ids must match the backend type names exactly, or the filter will return nothing.

sections.name: TimelinePage (part 1)
sections.title: Loading events and pinning
sections.what: Loads events and the summary at the same time, using the selected filter. Pinning saves the change, then updates the screen and shows a message. Failures are logged and, for loading, shown as a message.
sections.why: Loading both together keeps the page fast. The pin change is saved first so the screen reflects what is stored.
sections.watch_out: Unlike the records page, the pin screen update waits for the save, so a slow save makes the pin look delayed.

sections.name: TimelinePage (part 2)
sections.title: Search, grouping by date and page header
sections.what: Filters events by title or description text, groups the results under their date, and shows the header with a refresh button that spins while loading.
sections.why: Groups events by day so the timeline reads like a diary. Reason for the Recent label fallback is not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Grouping searches the group list for each event, which is fine for 100 items but slows down if the list grows a lot.

sections.name: TimelinePage (part 3)
sections.title: Four summary metric cards
sections.what: Shows four cards at the top of the timeline page: total records, records in the last 30 days, attention items (critical or severe events), and when the timeline was last updated. Values come from a summary object and show a dash or 'No records' when that data is missing.
sections.why: Gives the patient a quick overview before they scroll the event list.
sections.watch_out: The 'Synced with clinical datastore' text is fixed wording, so it does not prove the data was actually synced.

sections.name: TimelinePage (part 4)
sections.title: Category filter tabs and search box
sections.what: Draws the row of category buttons (highlighting the selected one) and a search box for finding events. Clicking a tab changes which kind of event is shown; typing updates the search text.
sections.why: Lets the patient narrow a long timeline by category or by keyword.
sections.watch_out: The search box only sets the search text here; the filtering logic that uses it lives elsewhere in the file and must stay in sync with these controls.

sections.name: TimelinePage (part 5)
sections.title: Loading, empty and feed states
sections.what: Shows a spinning icon while data loads, a friendly 'No Timeline Events Found' message when there is nothing to show, or otherwise a vertical timeline grouped by date.
sections.why: Makes sure the page always shows something sensible in each of the three states.
sections.watch_out: The empty-state check uses the grouped list, so if grouping breaks the page will wrongly look empty.

sections.name: TimelinePage (part 6)
sections.title: Event card content and badges
sections.what: For each event, draws a colored icon, the title, a type label, and a severity badge when the severity is not mild. Critical events get a red highlight, and pinned events get a highlighted border. A short description appears when one exists.
sections.why: Lets the patient spot important events at a glance by color and label.
sections.watch_out: Unknown event types fall back to the 'uploaded document' style, so a new event type may look like an upload unless it is added to the config.

sections.name: TimelinePage (part 7)
sections.title: Reading pills, time and pin button
sections.what: Shows vitals readings and medicine names as small tags on the card, the time of the event, and a pin button. Clicking the pin toggles whether the event is pinned, which changes its highlight.
sections.why: Lets the patient mark important events and see key numbers without opening anything.
sections.watch_out: The reading pill shows the value only when the metadata has one, so a missing unit or value will show a bare number or blank space.

summary: The Health Timeline page that lists a user's events (documents, vitals, medicines, symptoms, diagnoses, doctor notes) in date order, with search, filter tabs, pinning and a summary.
purpose: Gives the user one history view of their health events with a way to find and pin important ones.
why: Reason not fully stated in the code. Pinning is included so important events stay at the top of the user's view.
how: Loads up to 100 events and a summary from the backend, applying the chosen type filter on the server side. Search is applied in the screen to title and description. Events are grouped by date, and pin changes are saved to the backend with a message. Event type styles (icon, colour, label) come from a lookup table.
inputs: Events and summary from GET calls to /timeline and /timeline/summary, the selected filter tab, the search box text, and pin clicks.
outputs: Date groups of event items, a summary, a refresh button, and success or error messages.
risks: Only 7 of the 12 sections in this file were available for review, so the rest of the file is not described here. Pin changes are shown at once, and if the save fails the error is only logged, so the screen can show a pin that is not stored. The filter works on the server, but search only covers the loaded events.
debug: If events are missing, check the response from /timeline and whether the type filter matches the names in the filter list. If a grouping date looks wrong, check the occurredAt value from the backend. If pins do not stick, look at the PATCH call to /timeline/ id /pin.
